passage:
The demo was due at nine the next morning, and Rehana had four hours. Harish, her old college friend, leaned over. “Just send it to our batch group for feedback. They'll get it fast.”

She almost said yes. Then she noticed the word “our.” Everyone in that group thought like her, which was exactly why it felt easy. Instead she walked to Meera from the accounts team, who had never used the tool. Meera frowned at page two and asked, “Why would I trust this number?” Rehana fixed the label in ten minutes.

At the pantry, someone laughed about how the accounts team talks. Rehana set down her cup. “They stayed until two to close our numbers. Let's not.” Nobody answered, and Harish quietly refilled her tea.

qa.q: Why did Harish suggest sending the demo to the batch group?
qa.a: Harish thought the batch group would understand the demo fast.

qa.q: What did Rehana notice in the word “our” that made her stop?
qa.a: Rehana realised that everyone in that group thought like her, which was why it felt easy, and the ease made her doubt it.

qa.q: Which choice helped improve the demo, and how?
qa.a: Rehana asked Meera, who had never used the tool, and Meera's question about the number led to a quick fix of the label.

qa.q: How might Meera have felt when Rehana came to the accounts desk and later defended the team?
qa.a: Meera would probably feel respected, since Rehana sought Meera's honest view and stood up when the team was laughed at.

grounding: A mature adult checks a comfortable assumption, seeks a different view under time pressure and speaks up when a team is mocked, while staying friends with their college group.

passage:
At the colony's monthly meeting, Dhruv had already decided which way Vidya from the far block would vote. She always objected, he thought. Then he caught himself and asked her outright, “What worries you about the parking plan?” Vidya blinked. “The lane behind B block floods. Nobody has asked us.” It was a fair point he had missed.

Later, three men near the tea table joked about the security guards, mimicking how they speak. Someone laughed. Dhruv put his cup down. “They've watched over our children's cycles for years. Could we not?” One man shrugged, another looked at his shoes, and the laughing stopped.

Dhruv still walked home with his own block friends, chatting as usual. He just no longer needed them to be the only ones who mattered.

qa.q: What did Vidya say worries her about the parking plan?
qa.a: Vidya said the lane behind B block floods and nobody has asked the far block.

qa.q: Why did Dhruv ask Vidya outright about the parking plan?
qa.a: Dhruv felt uneasy on catching himself assuming Vidya would object, and was curious to hear Vidya's real reasons instead of guessing.

qa.q: What did Dhruv do when the joking about the guards began, and what happened next?
qa.a: Dhruv put his cup down and asked them to stop, mentioning the guards' years of watching over the children's cycles, and the laughing stopped.

qa.q: How might one of the guards feel if they had overheard the meeting that evening?
qa.a: They might feel relieved and quietly respected that someone in the group spoke up on their behalf, though the mocking would still sting.

grounding: A mature adult checks assumptions, asks a resident from another block for a view and speaks up when guards are mocked, while staying close to their own friends.
